description: Web-only overhaul of the session transcript reading experience: always render the session header/breadcrumb on the main transcript branch, add per-turn timestamps, syntax-highlight code blocks, introduce a turn TOC plus j/k/g/G keyboard navigation and a copy-full-text action, and harden the layout for 320–430px viewports. No server/runner/CLI/API/persistence changes.

tasks.title: Render SessionHeader on the main transcript branch, drop StickySessionTitle, and harden the header for narrow viewports
tasks.description:
Per design D1, replace the standalone `
{recoveryBar}
` at `SessionPage.tsx:759-789` (the turns>0 branch) with the same `` already used by the incomplete/waiting/empty branches (lines 709/725/746), so the main reading path always shows the breadcrumb, session title, status badge, workflow stage, issue back-link, and turn count, with `recoveryBar` rendered as a header sub-region. Remove `` from `SessionTranscriptLayout.tsx` and delete `StickySessionTitle.tsx` — the always-visible page header is a strict superset. Per design D7, harden the `SessionHeader` (defined at `SessionPage.tsx:267`) for narrow viewports: stack the metadata cluster vertically below `sm`, cap `issueTitle` with `truncate`, and apply `whitespace-nowrap` on the back-arrow + `Issue #N` link with `min-w-0` + `truncate` on the title so the row never wraps mid-link or overlaps.
acceptanceCriteria: The turns>0 main branch renders `<SessionHeader>` above the transcript scroll container, using the same props shape as the empty/waiting/missing branches.
On the main branch the header displays the session title, status badge, workflow stage, a link back to the owning issue, and the turn count.
`recoveryBar`, when present, renders inside the `SessionHeader` region on the main branch rather than as a standalone narrow strip.
The rendered main-branch header matches the header shown in the empty and waiting states (same component, same visual).
`StickySessionTitle.tsx` is deleted; `SessionTranscriptLayout` no longer references it and has no dangling imports; the layout becomes a pure turn list + streaming indicators.
Below the `sm` breakpoint the `SessionHeader` metadata stacks vertically, the issue title truncates, and the `Issue #N` back-link does not wrap mid-link or overlap at 320–430px.
Desktop (>=sm/md) header layout is visually unchanged from today.

New test (in a created or extended `SessionPage` test file) asserts the main branch renders the header with title/status/stage/issue-link/turn-count and `recoveryBar` inside the header region; existing branch behaviors remain green.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes.
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes.
tasks.output: Modified `packages/web/src/pages/session/ui/SessionPage.tsx` (main branch renders SessionHeader + responsive header classes), modified `packages/web/src/widgets/session-transcript/ui/SessionTranscriptLayout.tsx` (StickySessionTitle removed), deleted `packages/web/src/widgets/session-transcript/ui/StickySessionTitle.tsx`, and a created/extended `SessionPage` vitest file; all web tests green.
tasks.notes: Authoritative shape: design D1 + the header portion of D7 in openspec/changes/issue-243/design.md. The `SessionHeader` referenced here is the local function at SessionPage.tsx:267, NOT the coder-session widget. The design notes `SessionPage.test.tsx` already mocks `navigator.clipboard` and `Element.prototype.scrollTo` — if that file does not yet exist, create it alongside this task since later tasks (T-006) rely on the same clipboard mock pattern. Legacy `SessionTranscriptView.tsx` is explicitly out of scope (design Non-Goals) — do not delete it.

tasks.title: Display turn-level timestamps in the transcript layout
tasks.description: Per design D2, add a one-line turn header above `PromptBlock` inside `TurnItem` (`TurnList.tsx:29`) showing the 1-based turn index and a clock time derived from the always-present `DisplayTurn.startedAt` via `new Date(turn.startedAt).toLocaleTimeString()`, reusing the existing `formatTime` helper pattern from `AssistantParts.tsx:7`. Do not add a derived timestamp field to the model (`startedAt` IS the timestamp). Do not render the timestamp inside `PromptBlock` — prompt kinds like `legacy-missing` already render their own `sentAt` and would double-show.
acceptanceCriteria: Every rendered turn displays a visible timestamp in the normal reading flow, positioned above the prompt block within `TurnItem`.
The timestamp value is derived from `DisplayTurn.startedAt` (no new model field added).
Timestamp formatting matches the existing `formatTime` helper locale/time convention used in `AssistantParts.tsx`.
`legacy-missing` and other prompt kinds do not double-render timestamps (the turn header is the single source for the turn-level time).
New test asserts each turn in a multi-turn fixture renders a timestamp element whose text corresponds to that turn's `startedAt`.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes.
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes.
tasks.output: Modified `packages/web/src/widgets/session-transcript/ui/TurnList.tsx` (turn header with index + timestamp inside TurnItem) and extended `TurnList`/transcript tests; all web tests green.
tasks.notes: Authoritative shape: design D2. `DisplayTurn` already carries `id`, `startedAt`, `completedAt` plus prompt fields (`session-transcript-display.ts:107-115`) — this is presentation-only, no data plumbing. `completedAt` is intentionally left for the existing streaming indicator.

tasks.title: Syntax-highlight fenced code blocks via a shared TranscriptMarkdown component
tasks.description: Per design D5 (+ the TranscriptMarkdown overflow portion of D7), add `rehype-highlight` as a rehype plugin, importing the common-language subset via `lowlight/lib/common` (ts/js/bash/json/python/md/diff/yaml) rather than the full `highlight.js`. Create `widgets/session-transcript/ui/TranscriptMarkdown.tsx` — a thin wrapper around `react-markdown@10` + `remark-gfm@4` + `rehypeHighlight` carrying the current `code`/`pre` styling from `AssistantParts.tsx:31-48`, plus `overflow-x-auto` + `max-w-full` on the `pre` wrapper and `[overflow-wrap:anywhere]` on inline code so long lines/URLs no longer push width. Scope a single light theme (`highlight.js/styles/github.css`) under a `.transcript-md` wrapper class so it does not collide with `MarkdownReader`. Replace the inline `<Markdown>` in `AssistantTextPartView` with `<TranscriptMarkdown>`. Light theme only (no dark mode).
acceptanceCriteria: `rehype-highlight` (and `lowlight` if not transitive) is listed in `packages/web/package.json` dependencies.
`TranscriptMarkdown` is the single render path for assistant text in `AssistantParts`; the old inline `<Markdown>` is removed.
Fenced code blocks in assistant responses render with syntax-highlighted token spans; non-code markdown content renders unchanged.
`rehype-highlight` is configured with the `lowlight/lib/common` subset, not the full highlight.js grammar set.
The highlight theme CSS is scoped under a `.transcript-md` wrapper and does not leak into `MarkdownReader` or other markdown surfaces.
`pre` blocks scroll horizontally (`overflow-x-auto` + `max-w-full`) instead of overflowing the transcript column; inline code wraps via `[overflow-wrap:anywhere]`.
New test asserts a fenced code block renders highlighted output (e.g. presence of `hljs` token classes or a snapshot) while a non-code paragraph renders as before.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes.
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes.
tasks.output: New `packages/web/src/widgets/session-transcript/ui/TranscriptMarkdown.tsx`, modified `packages/web/src/widgets/session-transcript/ui/AssistantParts.tsx` (uses TranscriptMarkdown), updated `packages/web/package.json` (+ lockfile), and a TranscriptMarkdown test; all web tests green.
tasks.notes: Authoritative shape: design D5 + TranscriptMarkdown overflow slice of D7. Do NOT unify with the shared `MarkdownReader` in this change — design Non-Goals defers that to a separate cleanup issue; we only add highlighting to the transcript's bespoke markdown path. Candidate payload is ~30–50 KB gzipped; acceptable per design Risks. Rejected alternatives (shiki/rehype-pretty-code/prism-react-renderer) are documented in D5 — do not revisit.

tasks.title: Turn table of contents with shared turn-ref infrastructure, TranscriptToolbar, and card/grid responsive hardening
tasks.spec: specs/session-transcript-navigation/spec.md#Requirement: Transcript table of contents for turn navigation
tasks.description: Per design D3 (+ the card/grid portions of D7), introduce a `Map<number, HTMLDivElement>` of turn element refs keyed by 1-based index, owned by `SessionTranscriptLayout` and passed down: `<TurnList>` registers each turn's ref; consumers (`<TurnToc>`, keyboard hook in T-005) read refs by index. Render `<TurnToc>` from the same `displayTurns` array consumed by `<TurnList>` so streaming additions appear with no extra wiring; each entry shows the 1-based index plus a label derived from `prompt.kind` (e.g. 'Initial Task', 'Follow-up') and `prompt.title?.slice(0,60)`; clicking calls `scrollIntoView({ behavior:'smooth', block:'start' })` on the target ref. Placement: at `lg+` render a sticky right rail using a two-column `lg:grid-cols-[1fr_180px]` outside the existing `max-w-2xl` transcript measure; below `lg` render a compact 'Turns ▾' disclosure button in a new slim `TranscriptToolbar` above the turn list that opens an overlay reusing the same `<TurnTocList>`. Apply D7 card-width fixes: replace `max-w-[80%]`/`max-w-[90%]` with `max-w-[90%] sm:max-w-[80%]` and add `min-w-0` on card parents so truncation works at 320–430px. Add the cross-component 'no horizontal overflow at 320–430px' integration assertion here (faking `scrollWidth`/`clientWidth` getters on the container per D7, since jsdom cannot measure real layout) because this task introduces the layout-significant two-column grid.
acceptanceCriteria: TOC lists N entries for N rendered turns, in document order.
Activating the TOC entry for turn K calls `scrollIntoView` on the K-th turn's element ref (verified with a mocked `scrollIntoView`); boundary indices (first/last) are honored.
When a new turn arrives via the streaming path, a new TOC entry appears without a full page reload and without remounting existing entries.

At `lg+` the TOC renders as a sticky right rail inside a `lg:grid-cols-[1fr_180px]` layout that preserves the existing `max-w-2xl` transcript measure; below `lg` the rail is hidden and a 'Turns ▾' disclosure in `TranscriptToolbar` opens an overlay list reusing `<TurnTocList>`.
`TranscriptToolbar` is mounted above the turn list on the main branch and hosts the mobile TOC trigger (the copy-full-text button is added by T-006).
Turn refs map is keyed by 1-based index (not by `turn.id`), is owned by `SessionTranscriptLayout`, and is stable across streaming re-renders.
Prompt/assistant cards use `max-w-[90%] sm:max-w-[80%]` with `min-w-0` parents so content truncates rather than forcing horizontal overflow at 320–430px.
Integration test fakes `scrollWidth`/`clientWidth` getters and asserts `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` at 320/375/430px for a representative long-line transcript fixture.

New tests cover: TOC entry count == turn count, TOC click invokes scrollIntoView on the correct ref, streaming-appended turn appears in the TOC, mobile disclosure toggles the overlay, and responsive card classes are applied.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes.
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes.
tasks.output: New `packages/web/src/widgets/session-transcript/ui/TurnToc.tsx` (+ shared `TurnTocList`), new `packages/web/src/widgets/session-transcript/ui/TranscriptToolbar.tsx`, modified `SessionTranscriptLayout.tsx` (refs map + lg two-column grid + toolbar mount), modified `TurnList.tsx` (register refs + card responsive classes), and new tests; all web tests green.
tasks.notes: Authoritative shape: design D3 + card/grid slices of D7. Depends on T-001 because both rewrite `SessionTranscriptLayout.tsx` (T-001 removes StickySessionTitle; T-004 then adds the grid/refs/toolbar onto the cleaned layout) — sequencing avoids integration conflicts even though the design notes 'no ordering hazard' between rollout steps. Do NOT use `#turn-N` fragment navigation (rejected in D3: competes with React Router history and mis-scrolls inside the scroll container). Do NOT use IntersectionObserver (rejected in D3/D4: jsdom does not implement it). The no-overflow integration assertion is co-located here because the two-column grid is the most layout-significant change; header and TranscriptMarkdown overflow are covered by T-001/T-003 respectively, and the spec scenario 'No horizontal overflow on a narrow viewport' is satisfied at the change level once T-001 + T-003 + T-004 all land.

tasks.title: j/k/g/G keyboard navigation via useTurnKeyboardNav, deferring to focused inputs
tasks.description: Per design D4, add `useTurnKeyboardNav({ scrollContainerRef, turnRefs, turnCount })` in `widgets/session-transcript/model/`. It attaches one `keydown` listener on `scrollContainerRef.current` (falling back to `window`) on mount and detaches on unmount. It bails out (no-op) when `document.activeElement` matches `input, textarea, select, [contenteditable="true"], [data-composer-input]`, or when `event.metaKey`/`ctrlKey`/`altKey` are pressed — so the followup composer and modifier shortcuts are never hijacked. On a bare keystroke it computes the current turn index on demand by scanning `turnRefs` for the last element whose `getBoundingClientRect().top` is at/above ~120px from the top of the scroll container (no IntersectionObserver). `j` -> ref at index+1; `k` -> index-1; `g` (lowercase, no shift) -> ref at 0; `G` (`event.key === 'G'` OR `e.shiftKey && e.key === 'g'`) -> ref at turnCount-1. Boundary-clamped; out-of-range is a no-op. Calls `scrollIntoView({ block:'start' })` on the target ref and lets the existing `useSessionTranscript` `setIsNearBottom` reconcile the jump-to-bottom button. Wire the hook into `SessionTranscriptLayout` using the turn refs map introduced in T-004.
acceptanceCriteria: With no editable focused, `j` scrolls to the next turn (K -> K+1) and `k` scrolls to the previous turn (K -> K-1); boundary indices clamp so `j` at the last turn and `k` at the first turn are no-ops that do not scroll past the ends.
With no editable focused, `g` scrolls to the first turn and `G` (shift+g) scrolls to the last turn.

When the followup composer textarea (or any `input`/`textarea`/`select`/`[contenteditable]`/`[data-composer-input]`) is focused, `j`/`k`/`g`/`G` do NOT navigate and the focused input receives the keystroke as normal text entry.
Shortcuts do not fire when `metaKey`/`ctrlKey`/`altKey` are held.
The listener is scoped to the session transcript page (mounted only while the page is alive) and does not affect other pages.
Current-turn derivation uses `getBoundingClientRect` on demand at keystroke time (no IntersectionObserver, no jsdom polyfill required).
New tests cover j/k/g/G navigation, boundary clamping, focus-deferral (composer focused -> no nav), modifier-key suppression, and correct `scrollIntoView` target ref.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes.
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes.
tasks.output: New `packages/web/src/widgets/session-transcript/model/useTurnKeyboardNav.ts` (+ test), modified `SessionTranscriptLayout.tsx` (wires the hook with the T-004 turn refs); all web tests green.
tasks.notes: Authoritative shape: design D4. Depends on T-004 because it consumes the `turnRefs` map and `scrollContainerRef` wiring established there. `g` vs `G` is read from `event.key` (single keypress), NOT a timer-based 'press g twice' scheme. Rejected alternatives (IntersectionObserver scroll-spy, global hotkey library) are documented in D4 — do not revisit. Half-page / Space paging shortcuts are explicitly out of scope (design Open Questions).

tasks.title: Copy-full-transcript action with a pure serializer and surfaced failure handling
tasks.description: Per design D6, add a pure `serializeTranscriptPlainText(turns: DisplayTurn[]): string` to `widgets/session-transcript/model/`. For each turn in document order emit a header line (e.g. `== Turn N · <kind> · <timestamp> ==` using `startedAt`), the prompt title/subtitle/text, then each assistant part: text parts in full; reasoning summarized as `[reasoning omitted, X KB]` (consistent with 'reasoning collapsed by default'); tool parts as `[tool <name>] <title>`; errors as `[error] <message>`. Joined by blank lines. Add a `CopyFullTextButton` into the `TranscriptToolbar` (created in T-004), disabled when `turns.length === 0`. On click: compute the serialized text (memoized on the `turns` reference), call `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, flip the label to 'Copied!' for ~2s on resolve (matching the pattern at `PromptBlock.tsx:31`/`AssistantParts.tsx:24`), and on reject OR when `navigator.clipboard` is absent keep the label stable, fire `toast.error(...)` via `sonner`, and set `data-state="failed"` for tests — never report success on failure. Reuse the robust clipboard existence check from `ArtifactContentViewer.tsx:89` rather than a bare `.then(...)`.
acceptanceCriteria: `serializeTranscriptPlainText` is a pure function that, given a multi-turn `DisplayTurn[]` fixture, emits the expected plain-text document with one section per turn in document order (turn header line, prompt text, assistant text in full, reasoning omitted marker, tool summary lines, error lines).
The 'copy full text' button is disabled (or hidden) when `turns.length === 0`.
On a successful `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, the full serialized transcript is written and the button shows a success indication ('Copied!') for ~2s.
When `navigator.clipboard` is absent or `writeText` rejects, the UI surfaces the failure via `sonner` `toast.error`, sets `data-state="failed"`, and does NOT display a success indication.
The button reuses the robust clipboard-existence check from `ArtifactContentViewer.tsx:89` (no bare `.then` that silently swallows failure).
`CopyFullTextButton` is rendered inside `TranscriptToolbar` alongside the mobile TOC trigger.

New tests cover: serializer output for a representative multi-turn fixture (text/reasoning-omitted/tool/error), copy success path, copy failure path (clipboard absent + writeText reject) asserting `toast.error` and `data-state="failed"`, and disabled state for an empty transcript.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes.
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes.
tasks.output: New `packages/web/src/widgets/session-transcript/model/serialize-transcript.ts` (+ test), new `packages/web/src/widgets/session-transcript/ui/CopyFullTextButton.tsx`, modified `TranscriptToolbar.tsx` (mounts the button); all web tests green.
tasks.notes: Authoritative shape: design D6. Depends on T-004 for the `TranscriptToolbar` host and the `turns`/`displayTurns` reference already threaded through the layout. Per AGENTS.md testing rules: use fakes for `navigator.clipboard` and `sonner` toast — never real IO. The serializer format (reasoning omitted, tools summarized) is opinionated by design (D6 Risks); keep the function pure and unit-tested so the format is easy to extend later. Do NOT put the button inside `SessionHeader` (rejected in D6: would require threading turns into the header and re-checking empty-state across all four branches). Including full reasoning text behind a modifier is an Open Question, not in scope.
